scope: Source-only comparison using the same installed dependency tree; not a full release dependency comparison.
notes: All samples are retained, including exploratory resolver baselines and the outlier in the reverse-order run.
Resolver initialPair ran before then optimized tracked patch; commitPair ran optimized commit then before. Production resolver bytes match the committed revision.
Exploratory resolver runs predate phase timing and the audit CLI addition; compare their timing boundaries accordingly.
A11y exact-ID/cap/report-coverage validation and summaries were derived from recorded raw outcomes after timing; original timing values are unchanged.
Absolute checkout and temporary source paths are replaced with descriptive placeholders. Browser version, fixture hashes, counts, timings and process-memory samples are retained.

release.comparison: Source implementation comparison using one shared dependency installation; not a full release dependency comparison.
release.cachePolicy: Source trees have no generated dist/.out or project caches. OS filesystem caches are not flushed; workers document process and per-run cache resets.

preliminary.comparison: Source implementation comparison using one shared dependency installation; not a full release dependency comparison.
preliminary.cachePolicy: Source trees have no generated dist/.out or project caches. OS filesystem caches are not flushed; workers document process and per-run cache resets.

limitations: Cold means a fresh Node process, not a cleared operating-system filesystem cache.
Fixture creation happens before timing and writes every source file, warming filesystem caches.
Warm samples exclude module imports and one priming audit; they retain V8/module/filesystem warmth.
Combined audits reset their file-read cache each pass; standalone audits read every story each pass.
Cold timings include CLI formatting and process startup; warm timings include API work only.
Parser instrumentation runs separately from all timing samples. Base regex analyzers may report zero parses.
Different revisions may intentionally produce different findings; compare hashes within a revision before comparing timing.
The benchmark does not build Storybook, launch a browser, or evaluate consumer story modules.

methodology.profiles: Fresh Node worker for every sample, fresh Chromium browser for every real Pa11y check; no synthetic delays or browser reuse.
methodology.cache: No warmups are discarded. OS and filesystem caches can warm across samples. Cap order rotates between rounds.
methodology.timing: totalMs covers lintReportAndExit plus draining older early-rejecting runners. processWallMs additionally includes worker startup, imports, server startup and cleanup.
methodology.dependencies: Dependencies resolve from sourceRoot; nodeModulesRoot and its symlink state identify shared controlled dependency trees.
methodology.validation: Post-run validation against the generated index: exact requested/observed IDs, completed checks, cap adherence, and full output counts. Raw timing and memory observations unchanged.

browserMemory.scope: Sum of sampled RSS for launched Chromium roots and their current descendants; Node is excluded.
browserMemory.caveat: RSS double-counts shared pages and is not PSS. Sampling can miss short-lived or reparented processes and startup before launch resolves.
